import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# -------------------------------
# 1. Load the two input datasets
# -------------------------------
crime_path = "chunks_csv/getisord/getisord_crime_first_half_2013.csv"
adj_path   = "chunks_csv/borough_adjacency.csv"

crime_df = pd.read_csv(crime_path)                 # columns: borough, crime_rate_value
adj_df   = pd.read_csv(adj_path)                   # columns: borough, neighbor

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Build an undirected adjacency dictionary {borough: set()}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
neigh_dict = {b: set() for b in crime_df['borough']}

for _, row in adj_df.iterrows():
    b1, b2 = row['borough'], row['neighbor']
    neigh_dict.setdefault(b1, set()).add(b2)
    neigh_dict.setdefault(b2, set()).add(b1)       # make undirected

# ----------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Compute local sums  S_i  = borough i  + all its neighbours
#    Skip any borough whose own value is NaN (cannot be reported)
# ----------------------------------------------------------------
crime_series = crime_df.set_index('borough')['crime_rate_value']   # Series for fast lookup
local_sums   = {}   # borough -> local sum

for borough, own_val in crime_series.items():
    if pd.isna(own_val):
        continue                                   # drop boroughs with missing own value
    members = {borough} | neigh_dict.get(borough, set())
    # gather crime values, dropping NaNs automatically
    values  = crime_series.reindex(members).dropna().values
    local_sums[borough] = np.nansum(values)

# --------------------------------------------
# 4. Convert to array and compute z‐statistics
# --------------------------------------------
S_vals  = np.array(list(local_sums.values()))
mean_S  = np.nanmean(S_vals)
std_S   = np.nanstd(S_vals, ddof=1)

z_scores = {b: (s - mean_S) / std_S for b, s in local_sums.items()}

data_points_used = len(S_vals)

# ----------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Identify statistically significant HOT / COLD spots
# ----------------------------------------------------------
results = []
# First look at the stricter 99% threshold; if none, fall back to 95%
high_thr, low_thr = 2.576, -2.576
if not any((z > high_thr or z < low_thr) for z in z_scores.values()):
    high_thr, low_thr = 1.96, -1.96     # switch to 95%

for b, z in z_scores.items():
    if z > high_thr:
        results.append(f"{b} (HOT, z={z:.4f})")
    elif z < low_thr:
        results.append(f"{b} (COLD, z={z:.4f})")

# --------------------
# 6. Print the output
# --------------------
print(f"data_points_used = {data_points_used}")
if results:
    print(f"FINAL ANSWER: {', '.join(results)}")
else:
    print("FINAL ANSWER: none")
